A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VFScale. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite v4's expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original Maze and Sudoku experiments, including generalization, training ablations, inference comparisons and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds verifier comparisons, method variants, repeated-seed results, ranking analyses and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The default linear loss, KL regularizer, backbone and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. V4 adds optional adaptive BoN-to-MCTS switching based on branch-energy variance (D.3) and quadratic, rank-based and fixed-transformation loss variants (D.2). These extend components without replacing the core method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Maze size-generalization and SAT-Net-to-RRN Sudoku settings. The added experiments use the existing 15×15 Maze task; they introduce no new dataset, task or input-environment scenario.

E2.justification: V4 substantially expands comparisons with a learned external verifier for VFScale BoN, sparse and dense ground-truth verifiers for full VFScale hMCTS (Tables 10–11), and QRNCL, RBNCL and FTNCL loss variants (Table 12). V3's Original, DDPM and existing oracle comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Existing splits, training configurations, success metrics and matched-NFE comparisons are retained. Additional protocols compare verifiers on identical BoN candidates, measure Kendall tau across denoising steps 0–9, and profile peak memory and per-sample inference time (Tables 10, 19, 22–23). These supplement the original evaluation.

E4.justification: V4 adds analyses of verifier quality and reward density, alternative monotonic constraints, adaptive switching, permutation versus Gaussian negatives, and ranking alignment across denoising steps (Appendix D). V3's noise-scale, inner-loop and fixed-switch sensitivity studies remain, substantially expanding the questions tested.

E5.justification: V3 reports no run counts or uncertainty estimates. V4 introduces means and standard deviations over ten random seeds for key Maze comparisons (D.5/Table 18), plus mean and standard-deviation rank correlations (Table 19). This establishes new statistical reporting, not an increase from a documented earlier run count.

E6.justification: Earlier tabulated results are retained, while v4 adds substantial comparison, ablation, ranking and resource results. For example, Table 10 reports N=81 Maze success of 0.6562 with intrinsic versus 0.3203 with learned external verification; Table 18 newly reports N=81 hMCTS success of 0.8422±0.0147. These supplement rather than replace v3's headline scores.

T1.justification: The displayed core objectives, denoising equations, Appendix A consistency definition and linear-regression derivation are preserved apart from notation. V4's local-to-global discussion offers hypotheses and empirical evidence, without new formal assumptions, guarantees or proofs. Kendall tau is an added evaluation metric.

C1.justification: The training contribution broadens from specifically linear-regression NCL to monotonic-regression NCL, explicitly treating linear regression as its default instance. The main intrinsic-verifier and hMCTS contributions, task scope, and headline claims of approximately 88% Maze and 43% Sudoku success remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations of reduced single-sample performance as a scalability tradeoff, dense verification, structured negatives, and local constraints producing global ranking alignment (5.2 and Appendix D). Appendix F discusses quantified computational tradeoffs, and the contrastive-loss description changes from global to local minima. V3's standalone limitations paragraph is retained in Appendix I.

D1.justification: Appendix B.6 newly explains one-hot encoding, continuous denoising and argmax decoding; Appendix F adds memory and inference-time information. Appendix L explicitly states availability of datasets and pretrained checkpoints alongside code, whereas v3 already linked the same repository. These are additional disclosures, not established changes to the existing implementation.

R1.justification: The same 28 cited works and principal positioning relative to energy-based reasoning and externally verified diffusion scaling are retained. Updated titles, venues and author-year citation formatting do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized introduction and method rewrites, revises loss terminology, moves the experimental overview to Appendix B.1, and organizes appendix analyses into named subsections with a contents page. It adds acknowledgment and disclosure statements while retaining the main section sequence and much existing prose.

P2.justification: V4 substantially expands tables displaying verifier comparisons, variants, uncertainty, rankings and computational costs, and redraws Figure 2's intermediate states as continuous predictions. Existing plots and case studies remain with relocations, label updates and conference-format reflow. Table 21 redisplays training times already reported in v3's prose.

improvement.justification: V4 addresses important evidential gaps through ten-seed uncertainty estimates, direct verifier controls, and tests of alternative losses and negative sampling (Appendix D). Processing details and measured resource costs also improve reproducibility and assessment of computational tradeoffs (B.6/F). Some new claims that search success establishes global alignment exceed what the empirical tests demonstrate, but the substantial gains in validation and transparency outweigh this weakness.
